groups.text: It is currently cloudy and 14 degrees Celsius in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Researchers are finding that the problem-solving abilities of large language models often depend on textual formatting and context. To test this, Pavel Golikov and his colleagues introduced the Robust Reasoning Benchmark, which applies thirteen deterministic textual perturbations to AIME mathematical problems. While frontier models remained largely resilient, open-weights reasoning models showed significant failure modes, including reasoning collapse and accuracy drops of up to 54 percent. Some models also suffered from attention dilution, where intermediate reasoning steps polluted the context window. In a different application of machine learning, Yiming Qin and other authors have introduced DBMol to aid drug discovery. This new framework uses structure prediction models like Boltz-2 and AlphaFold-3 as background for designing small molecule ligands. By using an alternating optimization and projection process, DBMol aims to create target-specific molecules that bind with high affinity to specific protein pockets.

Remco Evenepoel has strengthened his second-place position in the Tour de France by winning the time trial of the sixteenth stage. The Belgian rider beat Tadej Pogacar by 28 seconds and Mattias Skjelmose by over a minute between Évian and Thonon, leaving him four minutes and 32 seconds behind the yellow jersey. In other sports news, Fabio Quartararo will move to Honda-HRC for the 2027 and 2028 MotoGP seasons after leaving Yamaha. Meanwhile, English referee Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement at age 47 following 831 matches. Shifting from professional circuits to local traditions, residents of Tirilbasa village in eastern India’s Jharkhand state recently held a football tournament featuring teams from 64 nearby villages. Organized to coincide with the FIFA World Cup, the event offered prize money and goats as trophies for the best-performing teams, with NCS Maudi winning the final against Kumbaram one-nil.

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports that Russia has lost an estimated 1,433,230 troops since February 2022, including 1,330 killed or wounded over the past twenty-four hours. This toll includes the loss of over twelve thousand tanks and more than four hundred thousand drones. While conflict persists in Ukraine, Germany is struggling to expand its own military capacity to meet NATO requirements. The Bundeswehr aims to grow by at least 75,000 personnel by 2035, but it is failing to attract women. Currently, women make up only 13.7 percent of the force, falling short of a 20 percent target. A report from the parliamentary commissioner for the armed forces notes that female applicants actually decreased in 2025. Young women in Berlin cite opposition to war, sexist environments, and conflicts with their professional or academic life as primary reasons for avoiding service.

Deutsche Bahn is implementing a ban on alcohol at all German railway stations by mid-October. The company points to successful test phases in Hamburg, Cologne, and Frankfurt, where conflicts decreased and passengers reported feeling safer. This policy follows two violent incidents: an attack on a ticket inspector last Friday and a fatal assault on a train attendant in February. While the newspaper DIE WELT supports the move, it warns that success depends entirely on having enough personnel to enforce the rules. In contrast, the TAZ argues that a ban limited to public areas around the tracks cannot prevent violent excesses. That publication further cautions that strict enforcement could trigger new conflicts, particularly if football fans resist alcohol checks and removals from the stations. Meanwhile, police union representatives note that federal police presence is already stretched thin by various large-scale events.

Developers are refining how AI tools handle errors and system resources. In the latest llama.cpp release, a server fix ensures that validation errors involving X-Conversation-Id now return a 400 error instead of a generic 500 crash. This change prevents empty sessions from lingering in memory when requests fail or do not stream. Additionally, the update stops the user interface from sending a backend sampling placeholder that previously caused default settings to fail validation. Meanwhile, PyTorch is addressing performance bottlenecks on macOS. Developers are skipping the inductor OpInfo CPU test for Mac users because it has consumed too many test-minutes and slowed down runner queue times. This specific adjustment targets macOS efficiency without affecting Linux or CUDA coverage for inductor amx. These separate updates reflect a broader effort to stabilize server responses and optimize hardware-specific testing cycles across open-source AI frameworks.

In Port Talbot, some residents live directly beneath an elevated section of the M4 motorway. This concrete monolith hangs about 45 feet above their plots on the main route between London and south Wales. Every day, roughly 75,000 vehicles travel over these gardens. For Narelle Cowan, three pillars of the highway stand in her back garden, where she uses one to hang her washing line. She notes that the structure acts as a sunshade during hot weather and keeps the back half of her garden dry. Aimee Lipley describes the overhead carriageway as a free gazebo that allows her to walk to local shops without getting her hair wet when it rains. This stretch of road is a relic of the 1960s freeway building boom, having opened on July 22, 1966, after a postwar explosion in car ownership.

Industrial chip design still relies heavily on manual refinement for macro placement, but a new framework called MAGE aims to automate this process using multimodal multi-agent reasoning. Developed by Andrew B. Kahng and his colleagues, the system uses natural-language directives and visual checks to mimic human expert designers. In tests across NanGate45 and GlobalFoundries 12nm enablements, MAGE outperformed commercial placers, showing geometric-mean improvements in TNS of up to 74 percent. This focus on specialized physical design contrasts with broader efforts to test general reasoning in large language models. Liam Swayne has introduced Relay-Bench, a text-only benchmark that requires models to solve composite problems across multiple domains in a single prompt. Even the leading model, GPT-5.5 xHigh, scored only 43.3 percent on these complex reasoning chains. While MAGE applies agentic logic to concrete hardware geometry, Relay-Bench reveals significant gaps in how general AI handles multi-domain problem solving.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 16 and 18 degrees Celsius.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has Nils Bauer's birthday and summer holidays in Berlin. Your work calendar has a team breakfast at half past nine, Optikrunde and a research sprint review at ten, MxM Spotlight at eleven, research sprint planning at half past one, and a group meeting with Gregor and an optional research seminar at three.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
